Hameln's Gnosis index is 22.46.

"22" refers to Piano Concerto No. 22 (K. 482), the second movement of which has a somber tone. "46" refers to Piano Concerto No. 20 in D minor (K. 466), which has a dark and dramatic tone. => Hameln's inner feelings

Additionally, number 246 could also refer to Mozart's Piano Concerto No. 8 in C major, composed in 1776 for Countess Antonia Lützow. The total performance time for all three movements is only about 20-22 minutes (significantly shorter than his later concertos). Mozart also used K. 246 as a teaching material for his piano students => Hameln also provided instruction for his less experienced music students at Mythag.

Hameln's birthday is September 21st.

It's mostly Derleth's take on The King in Yellow, where Hastur and Cthulhu is in some sort of war and that Cthulhu is water while Hastur is air, namely "The Return of Hastur" that integrated him into the Lovecraft universe, but it honestly is one of the worst Lovecraftian story known to mankind, so anyone after that that uses the King in Yellow pretty much just...ignored all that.
" please,morimens I need this my keepers kinda silverless"

I think the more recent notable works with King in Yellow has gone back to the root, where the King in Yellow could be just a fictional character in a play, a human in the real world pulling the string, or is an eldritch horror that might or might not exist, and unreliable narrator is a huge part of the story, I think True Detective and Signalis is pretty faithful to Chamber's version of the play itself.

Morimen is much more casual though so who knows what will happen.

I'm sure there's more work involving the King in Yellow that I can't remember for now, like a mind virus this guy can pop up in the most random of places. In some way the idea itself is perhaps the earliest example of a meme that has lived on in Lovecraftian literature, transforming itself in the process. This guy started out as some random god of shepherd of all things.
